stories.headline: Breece Hall Pulls Up Lame in Jersey and the Whole Saloon Holds Its Breath
stories.read: Hold up there, pardner, this is the one that moves your board. Hall caught a little swing pass Monday, nobody within ten feet of him, and went down clutchin' a groin before walkin' off with the trainers. Aaron Glenn says he don't think it was a big deal and they are sendin' him for pictures, so nobody go sellin' the ranch just yet. But a fella you were payin' second-round money for just got a question mark stapled to his saddle, so quit reachin' and let the herd blink first. The real play is the spare horses behind him: Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis are sittin' out there for pocket change, and if that groin talks back for even two weeks, whoever staked 'em first is haulin' free gold.

stories.headline: Hubbard's Hamstring Grabbed Him and Jonathon Brooks Just Got Handed the Reins
stories.read: Doc's been waitin' on this vein to open up. Dave Canales took Hubbard for an MRI after somethin' grabbed in one-on-ones, came back and called him week to week, and now Carolina's lead back misses the Buffalo exhibition with the opener a month out. They still expect him saddled for Week 1, so this ain't a funeral for Hubbard owners, but it is a wide open door. Jonathon Brooks gets the first-team work and the preseason start, and a young back gettin' the reins in August is exactly the kind of strike the saloon prices late. Go stake him now, before somebody in your outfit reads the same wire.

stories.headline: Egbuka's Toe Checks Out Clean and the Nervous Folks Are Handin' You a Discount
stories.read: Well now, here's free money if you got the nerve. Egbuka got rolled up on in the joint work with the Jets, limped off, missed the exhibition opener and skipped Monday's practice, which is exactly the sort of thing that spooks a greenhorn clean off a good claim. Trouble is the specialist looked at it and called the sprain stable, and Tampa's talkin' like he's fine for the opener. So the fellas you're ridin' against see a limp and slide him down their boards while you see a young fella in line for a big cut of the throws. That gap between the fear and the facts is where championships get bought.
